title:
Prices up.
Buyers gone.

lines.say: Singapore home prices just went up again. But almost nobody is buying.
lines.cap: home prices just went up again. but *almost nobody is buying*

lines.say: New home sales hit their lowest third quarter since nineteen ninety eight.
lines.cap: new home sales hit their *lowest Q3 since 1998*

lines.say: So why are prices still going up?
lines.cap: so *why are prices still going up?*

lines.say: Very few new launches. And seventh month kept buyers away.
lines.cap: *very few new launches*. and seventh month kept buyers away

lines.say: The homes that did sell were big tickets. Over seventy percent above two million.
lines.cap: the homes that did sell were big tickets. *over 70%* above $2M

lines.say: So the index rose because of what sold. Not because everyone rushed in.
lines.cap: the index rose because of *what sold*. not because everyone rushed in

lines.say: Outside the city centre, prices rose the most. Two point two percent.
lines.cap: outside the city centre, *prices rose the most*

lines.say: If you held an O C R condo right now, would you sell or hold?
lines.cap: holding an OCR condo right now. *sell or hold?* tell us why

source: source: URA flash estimate, 1 Oct 2026 · Huttons Asia
caption:
Prices went up. But new home sales just hit a 27 year low. 🤔

How can both be true? It comes down to what actually sold this quarter.

If you're holding an OCR condo right now, would you sell or hold? Tell us in the comments 👇
